summary: mountainash-transport follows a protocol-driven backend architecture where eight protocols define the storage contract, backends implement them a la carte, and the facade dispatches via isinstance checks. The settings pipeline flows from spec-driven profiles through typed adapters to SDK kwargs. Understanding these patterns and their invariants is key to maintaining and extending the package confidently.
use_cases: Add a new storage provider by creating a settings class, adapter, backend, and registry entry
Diagnose dispatch issues by tracing the scheme-to-provider-to-backend chain
Verify protocol conformance across all backends after modifying protocol signatures
Extend the settings pipeline with new authentication modes or provider-specific parameters
Maintain and evolve the S3 flavor dispatch as new S3-compatible services emerge

concepts.name: Protocol-driven backend contract
concepts.description: Eight runtime-checkable protocols define what a backend can do. Backends opt into protocols individually, and automated conformance tests verify alignment. This contract is the primary design invariant for the entire storage layer.

concepts.name: Backend registration and dispatch
concepts.description: The @register_storage_backend decorator maps provider types to backend classes. Path-to-provider detection resolves URL schemes to provider types, completing the dispatch chain from user input to concrete backend.

concepts.name: Mixin composition pattern
concepts.description: Local and S3 backends compose from per-protocol mixins, making it possible to add or modify protocol support in isolation. New backends can follow the same pattern by combining existing mixins with custom implementations.

concepts.name: Settings pipeline: Profile to Adapter to SDK kwargs
concepts.description: StorageProfile holds typed configuration fields. The to_handler_kwargs() method delegates to a provider-specific __adapter__ module that translates profile values into the exact kwargs the underlying SDK expects. Adding a new provider means writing one adapter function.

concepts.name: Spec-driven provider settings
concepts.description: StorageDescriptor declares provider metadata, required parameters, and supported authentication modes. The registry uses these specs for provider resolution, and new providers are added by defining a descriptor and decorating the settings class with @register.

concepts.name: S3 flavor dispatch
concepts.description: The S3 backend handles multiple S3-compatible providers through a FLAVOR discriminator that maps to provider-specific endpoint and region handling. Five provider types share one backend class, registered five times via stacked decorators.

concepts.name: Stream transform pipeline internals
concepts.description: The Pipeline class manages ordered transform application. apply_read and apply_write apply transforms in reversed order relative to each other, matching the outermost-first convention of stacked file extensions.

concepts.name: Scheme registry and path dispatch
concepts.description: The SCHEMES registry maps URL schemes to provider types with support for aliases and placeholder schemes for future backends. This is the entry point for all path-driven dispatch and the place to register new URL scheme support.

concepts.name: Test architecture
concepts.description: Tests are organized into protocol alignment tests (conformance and completeness verification), per-provider settings tests, and unit tests for core modules. The protocol alignment suite is the primary safety net for backend changes.

concepts.name: Cleanup opportunities
concepts.description: The settings.utils module contains partially commented-out code, and settings.templates may be eligible for removal after inlining. These are candidates for future cleanup to reduce maintenance surface.
